Where does Claude Code store session history, and how does Oh Agent read it?

Claude Code saves each session as a JSON Lines file under ~/.claude/projects/, one folder per project and one .jsonl file per session. Oh Agent reads those files on your Mac, without uploading them, and turns each session into a building in the Claude Code district of Agent City.

Key facts

Section titled “Key facts”
  • Location read: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl (all .jsonl files, recursively).
  • One file = one session. The file name (without .jsonl) is the session ID.
  • Live updates: Oh Agent watches ~/.claude/projects and picks up new or growing sessions.
  • Tokens counted: input, cache read, cache write and output tokens recorded in the log.
  • Read-only: Oh Agent does not modify or move Claude Code’s files.
  • Not followed yet: a custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR location (see below). You can add extra folders in Settings → Additional read locations.

Section titled “Where exactly are Claude Code sessions stored?”

On macOS the path is:

Each line in the file is one event in the conversation (messages, tool calls, token usage). Claude Code creates <project-folder> from the directory you started it in.

What does Oh Agent take from these files?

Section titled “What does Oh Agent take from these files?”

For each session Oh Agent records the time range, number of events and token counts, plus a short bounded title or task excerpt where available. Those feed the city: one building per session, with height from its total tokens. See What each building means.

The Agent City view never receives full prompts, file paths, working directories, tool arguments or raw errors. Raw conversation text stays in Claude Code’s own files. See Does Oh Agent upload my sessions?.

Why is my Claude Code district empty or smaller than expected?

Section titled “Why is my Claude Code district empty or smaller than expected?”
  • No sessions yet in the window. The desktop city shows the last 7, 30, 90 or 366 days; widen the window.
  • Old transcripts were cleaned up. Oh Agent can only show sessions whose log files still exist on this Mac. By default Claude Code deletes transcripts after 30 days; see Why are my older sessions missing?
  • Another device. History from other computers isn’t merged.
  • Custom config folder. If you set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, Claude Code stores session history there instead of ~/.claude (per Anthropic’s settings docs). Oh Agent 1.0.0-beta.2 doesn’t follow that variable. You can add extra folders in Settings, but they are read as <folder>/.claude/projects, so they don’t cover most custom config folders. TBD: confirm this behaviour; see Extra folders and manifest sources.
  • More than 4,000 sessions. The most recent 4,000 sessions in the window are loaded.
  • Permission. macOS may ask you to allow Oh Agent to read the folder.

Why are my older sessions missing from Agent City?

Section titled “Why are my older sessions missing from Agent City?”

Claude Code deletes old session transcripts by itself. Its cleanupPeriodDays setting defaults to 30 days, and the cleanup runs quietly in the background after a session starts. Oh Agent can only import sessions whose log files are still on your Mac. So if Claude Code removed a transcript before Oh Agent ever read it, that session can’t appear in Agent City, even in the 90- or 366-day window.

To keep more history, raise the value in ~/.claude/settings.json:

The value is a whole number of days, at least 1. 0 is rejected; for very long retention, Anthropic suggests a large value such as 3650. The setting only affects transcripts that still exist. It can’t bring back deleted ones.

Sessions Oh Agent has already imported stay in its own database after Claude Code deletes the log file. They are removed by Oh Agent’s own retention (13 months by default) or when you delete a source’s data in Settings. TBD: confirm on a real install that already-imported sessions still appear in the City after their log file is gone.

Do I need an API key or to be logged in?

Section titled “Do I need an API key or to be logged in?”

No. Oh Agent reads files Claude Code already wrote. It needs no Anthropic API key and no Oh Agent account.
